request.prompt: Which humanoid robots can be purchased in Europe?

result.text:
As of October 2026, several humanoid robots can be purchased through European distributors, including in Germany. The market has moved beyond experimental prototypes: you can now order walking, programmable humanoid robots for research, education, demonstrations and, in some cases, personal use.

The available models range from approximately €4,000 to over €200,000.

Here are the most interesting options.

1. Humanoid robots currently available in Europe

Indicative European retail prices. Prices depend on configuration, VAT, shipping and availability.

1. Unitree R1

€4,500–10,500

Entry-level option

Compact, lightweight humanoid

Walking, running and basic movements

Suitable for experimentation and education

Available through European robotics retailers

Also available in EDU configurations.

2. Unitree G1

€18,000–30,000

Strong all-round choice

Approximately 127–132 cm tall

Dynamic walking and sophisticated movements

AI and computer vision capabilities

Programmable through development interfaces

EDU versions offer more development possibilities

One of the most accessible serious humanoid development platforms.

3. Booster K1

€9,000–20,000

Compact humanoid research platform

Designed for robotics education and development

Walking, movement and AI experimentation

Different hardware configurations available

4. Noetix Bumi

€5,000–8,000

Small humanoid form factor

Educational and research applications

More affordable entry into humanoid robotics

Not a general-purpose household assistant

5. Fourier GR-1

€38,000–112,000

Full-size humanoid, approximately 165 cm

Human-like body proportions

Research into manipulation and human interaction

More advanced research platform

6. Fourier GR-2

€75,000–200,000+

Advanced full-size humanoid

More sophisticated manipulation capabilities

Research, development and human-robot interaction

Primarily aimed at institutional and commercial buyers

7. Unitree H1 / H2

€50,000–120,000+

Full-size humanoid platforms

Advanced dynamic locomotion

Industrial and research applications

More substantial hardware than the G1

Prices are indicative ranges rather than guaranteed quotations. European listings include configurations with very different sensors, hands, software and development capabilities.

2. More advanced and specialised humanoids

These are also worth investigating, although purchasing often requires a direct commercial enquiry.

NEURA 4NE1

€20,000–100,000+

German manufacturer. Industrial and service robotics, human interaction and cognitive AI.

Manufacturer website

AGIBOT X2

€22,000–55,000

Compact humanoid designed for service, interaction and robotics development.

Manufacturer website

Ameca

Price on request

Highly expressive face, realistic gestures and human interaction. Particularly interesting for exhibitions and public-facing applications.

Manufacturer website

Booster T2

€30,000–130,000+

Advanced research and development platform with more sophisticated manipulation options.

Manufacturer website

3. Where can you buy them in Europe?

These are some useful purchasing channels:

Retailer / distributor

Main offering

RobotShop EU

Unitree humanoids

RBTX

Unitree, Fourier, AGIBOT, Booster and others

Terra Robotics

Unitree and other robotics platforms

Funduino

Robotics and humanoid development platforms

Reichelt

Selected humanoid robots

Sonny Robotics

Several humanoid platforms

For Germany, I would start with RobotShop EU, RBTX, Terra Robotics and Reichelt.

Further market comparisons: Robot Distribution humanoid catalogue .

4. Which would I choose?

Intended application

My recommendation

Affordable humanoid experimentation

Unitree R1

Serious robotics development

Unitree G1 EDU

University or research laboratory

Unitree G1 / Fourier GR-2

Human interaction and exhibitions

Ameca

Industrial automation research

NEURA 4NE1 / Unitree H1

Advanced manipulation research

Fourier GR-2

One important distinction: Most commercially available humanoids are still robotics development platforms. They cannot yet reliably perform all the tasks of a human assistant, such as cooking, cleaning, doing laundry or independently managing a household.
